title: Biological Foundation Models — records under review
description: Audited candidates excluded from the displayed canonical index until their scope, artifact, identity, duplication, or reuse-term issue is resolved.

policy.promotion_rule: A record may move into models_final.json only after the stated reconsideration condition is met, primary evidence is refreshed, and the full maintenance gate passes.

record.name: DeepSEA
record.description: Pioneering deep-learning sequence model that predicts 919 chromatin features (TF binding, DNase, histone marks) from DNA with single-nucleotide sensitivity to prioritize noncoding variants.
record.io: DNA sequence (~1 kb) -> 919 chromatin feature predictions; noncoding variant effect scores
record.status: HOLD: no written historical-exception policy; the original 2015 release host (deepsea.princeton.edu) was not serving DeepSEA on 2026-10-10; no licence was stated for the original download; successor Sei is catalogued as bfm-sei
record.use_cases: Noncoding/eQTL/disease variant prioritization, chromatin feature prediction, regulatory sequence analysis

code_links.label: Selene framework (DeepSEA architecture definition; not the original 2015 trained-model release)

record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The original release page located on 2026-08-13 (deepsea.princeton.edu/help/) now returns 404/503, and the site root serves a default server test page. HumanBase DeepSEA (official lab server) serves Sei (2021) and Beluga (2019), not the 2015 model. Selene holds a DeepSEA architecture definition only. No historical-exception policy has been adopted. The '919 features' and '~1 kb' claims are inherited and were not re-verified (paper paywalled). The journal label was corrected from 'Nature' to 'Nature Methods'.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Scope: no written historical or supervised-predictor exception policy exists (MAINTENANCE.md unchanged since 2026-07-14). Artifact: the original 2015 release host located in August (deepsea.princeton.edu/help/) now returns 404/503, and the site root shows a default server test page. The lab's live HumanBase DeepSEA server offers Sei and Beluga, not the 2015 model, and Selene contains only a DeepSEA architecture definition. Sei is already displayed as bfm-sei. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if (a) a written historical-exception or supervised multi-task predictor policy is adopted in MAINTENANCE.md and (b) an official, currently reachable copy of the original 2015 DeepSEA trained model (lab server, HumanBase download or official archive) is identified with its terms recorded. If (a) holds but (b) fails, consider retiring in favour of bfm-sei.

record.name: ChromBPNet
record.description: Kundaje-lab bias-factorized, base-resolution CNN of chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq/DNase-seq), trained for each dataset. A frozen pretrained enzyme-bias model is combined with a trainable TF sub-model to reveal motif syntax, TF footprints and regulatory variant effects.
record.io: DNA sequence -> base-resolution accessibility profiles; TF motif/footprint and variant-effect outputs
record.status: HOLD: MIT code; CC-BY-4.0 reference bias models on Zenodo; per-dataset trained models on ENCODE/Synapse (terms there not checked); no single broadly pretrained model
record.use_cases: cis-regulatory syntax discovery, TF footprinting, regulatory variant scoring, enhancer/accessibility modeling
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10 against preprint v4 (2026-09-23), README, licence, releases and the Zenodo bias-model deposit. Per-dataset predictor with a transferable bias component; no broad reusable pretraining and no scope policy for assay-specific predictors.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The preprint was revised to v4 (2026-09-23; still not journal-published) with an unchanged abstract. The full text describes a lightweight model trained on each dataset, with a frozen pretrained enzyme-bias component, and treats 'foundation' models as future work. The reusable artifacts are MIT code, CC-BY-4.0 reference bias models on Zenodo (transferable within an assay type) and per-dataset trained models on ENCODE/Synapse. No broad reusable pretraining is evidenced, and no written policy covers assay-specific predictors. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider if a written scope policy explicitly admits assay-specific sequence-to-function predictors or model compendia of per-dataset checkpoints, or if the developers release and document a single pretrained ChromBPNet-family model intended for reuse across datasets or cell contexts.

record.name: Mistral-DNA
record.description: Family of small causal DNA language models by Raphaël Mourad that reduce the Mixtral-8x7B mixture-of-experts architecture for genomics. Public v1 checkpoints (1M-422M parameters) are pretrained on hg38 (10 kb sequences), with further checkpoints named for bacterial, yeast, Arabidopsis, viral and other corpora.
record.io: DNA sequence -> embeddings, next-token likelihoods (zero-shot variant scores), generated DNA; fine-tuned classification heads
record.status: HOLD: public ungated checkpoints with apache-2.0 model cards; repository code has no licence; no primary paper or technical report; README still links a non-public v0.1 checkpoint
record.use_cases: Genomic sequence classification, DNA generation, fine-tuning for regulatory/variant tasks, teaching/tutorials
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Authorized checkpoint, direct model card and weight terms verified (v1 hg38 cards: apache-2.0, ungated, safetensors). The README-linked v0.1 checkpoint returns 401. Code repository has no licence. No primary paper or technical report was found (Europe PMC, arXiv, web search). GTN tutorials co-authored by the developer document reuse only.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Three of the four sub-conditions are now met: the developer's account has 15 public, ungated Mistral-DNA-v1 checkpoints with direct model cards, and the hg38 cards checked declare apache-2.0. Still missing: a primary paper, preprint or technical report describing the released v1 checkpoints. The GitHub code has no licence file, and the README still links a v0.1 checkpoint that returns HTTP 401. Developer co-authored Galaxy Training Network tutorials document reuse of v1-17M-hg38 but are not a model report. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider when a developer-authored primary description (paper, preprint or technical report/release note) of the released Mistral-DNA-v1 checkpoints (training corpus, objective, evaluation) is verified, or when the curator records in writing that developer-authored GTN tutorials plus model cards suffice as primary documentation. Checkpoint, model-card and weight-terms evidence was verified on 2026-10-10 and should be spot-checked again at promotion.

record.status: HOLD: MIT code; the official pretrained weights (Google Drive) returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-10; Hugging Face copies are third-party uploads; preprint only
record.use_cases: Cross-species gene-expression prediction from promoters, promoter representation learning, crop transfer learning
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Corrected against the preprint: about 7.9M pretraining sequences (not ~11.7M), 93 plant species, 9 maize tissues (not 8). review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if the authors restore an official, reachable weight release with stated terms and primary evidence shows the plant-promoter language model being reused beyond maize tissue-expression regression.

record.name: DRfold
record.description: End-to-end deep-learning RNA tertiary-structure predictor combining learned local frame rotations and geometric restraints (MSA-free); DRfold2 (2026) adds a pretrained RNA Composite Language Model (RCLM) and a denoising structure module for end-to-end ab initio folding.
record.io: RNA sequence (+ secondary structure) -> predicted 3D tertiary structure (atomic resolution)
record.status: HOLD — catalog eligibility or reusable-artifact evidence is unresolved; see audit note
record.use_cases: Ab initio / single-sequence RNA 3D structure prediction without MSA
record.audit_note: DRfold/DRfold2 are RNA structure predictors; DRfold2 contains a pretrained RCLM component, but the catalogue record itself remains one-task structure prediction. HOLD or define a structural-model exception. DRfold paper, DRfold2 paper, DRfold, DRfold2. Re-reviewed 2026-08-13 (evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_2.json): the successor repository does ship reusable artifacts - its install script downloads about 1.3 GB of model weights under MIT-form terms - but the weight locator is indirect and both remaining paths are curatorial: no written structural-model exception exists, and the record still frames the entry as one-task RNA structure prediction rather than around the pretrained language-model component.

review.reason: Residual from the 2026-10-10 split. The pretrained RCLM component was promoted under bfm-drfold. DRfold (2023, Nature Communications) remains a single-task RNA tertiary-structure predictor with no pretrained language-model component. Its readme gives mixed terms (all rights reserved, MIT use) and the repository has no LICENSE file. No written structural-model exception exists. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if MAINTENANCE.md adopts a written structural-model exception. That exception should also settle the displayed trRosettaRNA, RhoFold+ and RNAPro records consistently. Otherwise consider retiring the residual as out of scope.

record.io: Protein sequence -> predicted compartment / mutation effect on localization; or compartment target -> generated sequence
record.status: HOLD: task-specific localization classifier and conditioned generator; MIT code and CC BY 4.0 checkpoints exist, but broader foundation-model scope is not established
record.use_cases: Subcellular/condensate localization prediction, disease-mutation localization-shift analysis, generative design of compartment-targeted proteins
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The artifacts exist: MIT code, a GitHub v0.0.1 release (model.zip, dataset.zip), and Zenodo 14795445 (CC BY 4.0, checkpoints.zip). The released configuration trains a 12-class multilabel compartment classifier on esm2_t6_8M_UR50D, and generation runs through ESM lm-design scripts. No broader foundation-model scope is documented and no written task-specific exception exists. The Science page returned 403; the abstract was read via Europe PMC. Year corrected to 2024 (bioRxiv preprint posted 2024-04-17).

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. ProtGPS remains a task-specific model: a 12-class compartment/condensate classifier fine-tuned from esm2_t6_8M_UR50D, plus classifier-guided generation. MIT code and CC BY 4.0 Zenodo checkpoints exist, but no broader reusable foundation-model scope is documented and no written task-specific exception has been adopted. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if MAINTENANCE.md adopts a written task-specific exception, or if the authors release and document ProtGPS as a general-purpose representation model evaluated beyond localization.

record.name: Uni-Mol Docking V2
record.description: Docking-specific model trained from the pretrained Uni-Mol molecule and pocket encoders that predicts protein-ligand binding poses. It reports 77+% of PoseBusters ligands under 2 Å RMSD with chemically valid poses that avoid chirality inversions and steric clashes.
record.io: Protein pocket + ligand -> binding pose 3D coordinates
record.status: HOLD — scope: single-task docking pose predictor. MIT code, a 464 MB checkpoint linked from the README (Dropbox) and a hosted Bohrium app exist, but MAINTENANCE.md has no written structural/docking exception.
record.use_cases: Binding-pose prediction, structure-based virtual screening, lead optimization
record.audit_note: Exact model is a dedicated docking predictor rather than an unambiguous broader-than-one-task FM. HOLD or document a structural/docking exception. Paper, repo.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. Identity and artifacts verify: MIT code, a README-linked 464 MB checkpoint, a hosted Bohrium app, the arXiv preprint and a new ICANN 2025 LNCS chapter. Every primary source still describes a single-task protein-ligand pose predictor, and its reusable encoders are already catalogued as bfm-uni-mol. MAINTENANCE.md contains no written structural/docking exception. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider only if MAINTENANCE.md adopts a written structural/docking exception (applied consistently with displayed docking-adjacent records such as bfm-flowdock), or if an official release documents reuse beyond binding-pose prediction. If maintainers decide against a docking exception, retire rather than re-hold.

record.name: ScDiVa
record.description: Masked discrete-diffusion single-cell foundation model (12-layer bidirectional transformer, about 94.5M parameters) that jointly models gene identity and continuous expression magnitude with a latent anchor token; pretrained on 59 million cells.
record.io: Masked/corrupted single-cell expression -> denoised gene identities + magnitudes, cell embeddings, generated cells
record.status: HOLD — Apache-2.0 code and ungated Apache-2.0 weights; the corrected GitHub loader matches the hub checkpoint, but the 41,818-gene vocabulary needed to tokenize new data is not released and the hub-hosted loader is outdated
record.use_cases: Single-cell generation, dropout/sparsity-aware denoising, joint identity-and-expression modeling, representation learning
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The September loader defect is fixed on GitHub: scdiva/modeling_scdiva.py reads model.safetensors with safetensors.load_file, pins config and weights to one hub revision and loads strictly with no random-init fallback; the safetensors header of the unchanged hub checkpoint (128 tensors, 94.5M parameters) matches every parameter name and shape in that code. Checked statically; nothing was downloaded or executed. Still missing: the 41,818-gene vocabulary or tokenizer needed to encode new data (absent from the GitHub tree, the hub model files and the hub dataset). The hub model card and hub-hosted modeling_scdiva.py still show the superseded loader that falls back to random weights. Unrelated scDIVA methods remain distinct (arXiv 2602.03477).

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10: the corrected GitHub loader (safetensors + strict loading, revision-pinned) statically matches every tensor name and shape in the hub checkpoint header, and code and weights are Apache-2.0, so the September loader condition is met. The released checkpoint still cannot be applied to new data: the 41,818-gene vocabulary (gene to token-ID mapping) or tokenizer that the model card requires is not published in the GitHub repository, the hub model repo or the hub dataset. The hub-hosted loader and model card still show the superseded random-init-fallback loader. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Promote when an official source (GitHub or the hub repo) publishes the 41,818-gene vocabulary or tokenization code that maps new expression data to the checkpoint's gene IDs. Record then as Apache-2.0 code and weights, noting in the audit note if the hub model card still shows the superseded loader. Keep disambiguation from unrelated scDIVA methods.

record.name: Atlas (RudolfV successor)
record.description: Aignostics/Mayo Clinic/Charité pathology foundation model (ViT-H/14, 632M parameters) built on the RudolfV approach and trained on 1.2M WSIs spanning over 70 tissue types and over 100 stain types. The line has since advanced to Atlas 2 (arXiv 2601.05148): a 2B-parameter ViT trained on 5.5M WSIs from Charité, LMU Munich and Mayo Clinic, with distilled 2-B and 2-S variants.
record.io: Histology tile -> tile-level embedding
record.status: HOLD — no public Atlas or Atlas 2 weights or documented API; Atlas 2 is offered only through commercial piloting/licensing inquiries, and the vendor's open-access line is the separately tracked RudolfV-2 family
record.use_cases: Pan-tissue cancer classification, biomarker prediction, WSI feature extraction across diverse stains/scanners
record.audit_note: Held since 2026-07-13: the originally listed model-hub artifact is absent. Re-reviewed 2026-08-13, 2026-09-11 and 2026-10-10. In October the Aignostics hub organisation lists only RudolfV-2/-S/-B, and the product page offers Atlas 2 by licensing inquiry only. Training-data and architecture facts were re-verified against arXiv 2501.05409, and Atlas 2 facts against arXiv 2601.05148 v2. RudolfV-2 is a separate candidate, not evidence for Atlas. Evidence: evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_3.json; October hold batch 8.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10: there is still no public Atlas or Atlas 2 artifact or documented endpoint. The Aignostics hub organisation lists only the RudolfV-2 family (gated, tracked separately as bfm-rudolfv-2). The official foundation-models page offers Atlas 2 only through piloting or licensing inquiries, and it presents RudolfV 2 as the open-access academic line and Atlas 2 as the commercial one. Neither the Atlas report (arXiv 2501.05409) nor the Atlas 2 report (arXiv 2601.05148 v2, 2026-07-24) states weight or API availability. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Aignostics publishes Atlas or Atlas 2 weights, or a documented public API/endpoint with readable access terms. A sales or licensing-inquiry form does not count, and RudolfV-2 evidence must not be substituted. If Atlas 2 is still offered only by commercial licence inquiry at the next review, the maintainer should decide whether to retire this record as lacking a reusable access route.

record.name: BioReason
record.description: Architecture that embeds a DNA foundation model (Evo2/Nucleotide Transformer) directly into an LLM so the LLM reasons over raw genomic sequence as a first-class input via SFT + RL, producing interpretable multi-step reasoning.
record.io: Raw DNA sequence + text question -> multi-step biological reasoning / variant-effect / pathway answer with explanation
record.status: HOLD — Apache-2.0 code and Apache-2.0 datasets are public; README still says checkpoints will be released soon and no official checkpoint is on the model hub
record.use_cases: Mechanistic variant-effect explanation, KEGG disease-pathway reasoning, interpretable genomics QA
record.audit_note: repository still says checkpoints are forthcoming. HOLD until a reusable checkpoint is released. Re-reviewed 2026-08-13 (evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_3.json): the promised checkpoints are still unreleased - the README's checkpoint section reads that they will be released soon, while the abstract in the same file continues to claim public checkpoints - and no model-hub artifact exists. The successor BioReason-Pro has been released separately and is already a displayed record; it is a different model and does not lift this hold.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10: the bowang-lab/BioReason README checkpoint section still says the checkpoints will be released soon, the official HF 'BioReason' collection lists only three Apache-2.0 datasets, and no wanglab model repository holds BioReason DNA-LLM checkpoints (matches are BioReason-Pro, already displayed, and an empty, manually gated BioReasonCell placeholder for a different single-cell model). Code is Apache-2.0 and the paper is now a NeurIPS 2025 proceedings article, but no reusable model artifact exists. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Official BioReason (DNA-LLM) checkpoints are linked from the bowang-lab/BioReason README or appear as wanglab model cards with weight files. Then verify the weights licence and gating, and check whether Nucleotide Transformer-based variants inherit upstream non-commercial terms (set noncommercial accordingly). BioReason-Pro, BioReasonCell or gene-pathway SFT repositories do not satisfy this condition.

record.name: Pearl
record.description: Protein-ligand co-folding foundation model from Genesis Molecular AI that combines large-scale synthetic training data, an SO(3)-equivariant diffusion module and controllable multi-chain templating. Its technical report claims 14.5% (Runs N' Poses) and 14.2% (PoseBusters) gains over the next-best model.
record.io: Protein sequence + ligand chemical structure (optional protein/ligand templates or pocket conditioning) -> co-folded all-atom protein-ligand 3D structure
record.status: HOLD — technical report verified; Pearl is deployed only in Genesis' internal pipeline, partnership programs and its GEMS platform; no public weights, code, API or terms verified
record.use_cases: Structure-based drug discovery, binding-pose prediction, pocket-conditioned co-folding
record.audit_note: Only a paper is cited; “Web/API/commercial” lacks an official artifact locator. Official Genesis pages describe Pearl and an AI platform/partner access, not a public model endpoint. Paper, official Pearl page. Re-reviewed 2026-08-13 (evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_3.json): paper identity was confirmed, but no artifact or terms exist to verify - the vendor's research page describes the model without stating access, weights, API or licensing, dedicated product paths return not-found, and the public inference catalogue lists no matching entry. A vendor endpoint path returns HTTP 200 for arbitrary paths, so it is worthless as evidence; a public endpoint remains unverified rather than confirmed absent.

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The technical report (arXiv 2510.24670) and official Genesis pages verify identity, but Pearl remains internal, partner-only and GEMS-platform technology. The Genesis Hugging Face and GitHub orgs and the DeCAF hub files hold no Pearl weights, code or endpoint, and no public terms exist. A new June 2026 benchmark post did not change access. Re-reviewed 2026-10-10; see evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.
review.reconsider_when: Reconsider when Genesis releases Pearl weights or code, or documents a public or self-serve Pearl API with stated terms. Partner-only or GEMS-platform access does not qualify.

record.status: HOLD — public code and Google Drive checkpoints (2M, 160K, 10K and one fine-tuned), but the README states Tencent AI Lab copyright, all rights reserved, with no reuse licence; scope as a single RNA-to-protein translation model is unresolved
record.use_cases: Proteome inference from RNA-only data, cross-technology RNA-to-protein translation, downstream interaction inference, pseudo-knockout, clustering and batch correction on translated profiles

review.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10: terms are now explicit. The README says 'The copyright holder for this project is Tencent AI Lab.
